A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Transformers are Inherently Succinct. All 16 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v3, including their proof appendices and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical constructions, succinctness bounds, and complexity proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 remains entirely theoretical, including its appendices. Its discussion of empirical learnability evidence attributes that evidence to other work.

M1.justification: The UHAT architecture, affine/ReLU operations, masking and tie-breaking options, and tiling-based construction remain. v3 expands the existing compilation construction and clarifies acceptance conventions without establishing a different underlying method.

E1.justification: Neither version trains or evaluates on datasets or experimental tasks. The formal languages and tiling instances serve as mathematical witnesses.

E2.justification: LTL, finite automata, and RNNs remain theoretical comparison formalisms. Neither version evaluates empirical baseline methods.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets, or evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses. Revised illustrative constructions are part of the mathematical development.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: Neither version reports empirical numerical results or experimental findings. Changes to mathematical bounds and their formulation are assessed under T1 and C1.

T1.justification: Section 2.5 replaces v1's exclusion of every subexponential bound with witness-family bounds allowing 2^(c n^d), including d below 1, and introduces bounded expansion. v3 also generalizes and develops the B-RASP-to-UHAT translation in Lemma 9/Appendix A.3, adds counter-initialization and size-conversion reasoning to Theorem 15, and corrects the LTL example and tiling encoding. These are substantive formal revisions beyond proof relocation.

C1.justification: The headline succinctness gaps and EXPSPACE-completeness claims remain. However, v3 explicitly frames the separation through polynomial-size witness families, and its revised definition permits stretched-exponential dependence on representation size, weakening the precise meaning of v1's exponential claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive qualifications about floating-point nonassociativity and deterministic evaluation order, and about EOS-padding effects on restricted LTL. Section 6 newly discusses counter-restricted verification, unresolved learnability, and the remaining succinctness questions for softmax and average-hard attention.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly documents one-hot initialization, affine/ReLU implementations of Boolean operations, the attention-score construction, and conditional default handling for the existing reduction. These improve construction-level reproducibility; neither version supplies software, hardware specifications, or experimental implementation details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting arithmetic qualifications, RNN background, padding sensitivity, learnability, and recent transformer verification results, including Goldberg (1991), Li and Cotterell (2026), and Salzer et al. (2026). It removes the Zipf analogy while retaining the central positioning against earlier UHAT and verification work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The appendix is reorganized into seven proof subsections, with explicit construction stages, revised terminology, clearer cross-references, and proofs moved from the main text.

P2.justification: Both retain a single-column, text-and-equation presentation without figures or tables. v3 adds systematic equation numbering, reformats equation groups, expands footnotes, and changes proof placement and bibliography formatting.

improvement.justification: v3 improves clarity and auditability through explicit compilation steps, better witness-size reasoning, and clearer applicability qualifications. The gain is limited by remaining mathematical issues: the expanded precision proof in Appendix A.4 newly bounds scaled coefficient bit-length by log D alone, omitting the original numerator size. The revision improves documentation without delivering a comprehensive mathematical repair.
